summary: Marguerite E. Adiceam was an Indologist who studied at the University of Lyon and under Jean Filliozat. She taught at the Lycée Français de Pondichéry (1946–1954) and was a scientific member of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1966–1971).

Marguerite Lobsiger-Dellenbach worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, earning a Ph.D. from the University of Geneva. She served at the Musée d'ethnographie de Genève as Vice-Director in 1947 and Director from 1952 to 1967, succeeding Eugène Pittard.

Maria Byrski is an Indologist who studied under Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz. He taught Bożena Śliwczyńska and Danuta Stasik, and served as Head of the Indology Department at the University of Warsaw from circa 1990 to 1996.

Maria Carlotta Avanzi specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She studied at the University of Turin and Kyoto University, becoming Associate Professor at Akita Prefectural University in 2021 and Assistant Professor at the Italian School of East Asian Studies (attested 2026).

Maria Elisabeth Lulius van Goor was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Leiden University under Jacob Samuel Speyer. She served as attachée at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1922–1923) and Praeceptor of Pāli at Leiden University (1924).

Maria Gallas is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. She earned a master's degree in philosophy from the National University of Distance Education (2019–2022) and is a PhD student at Universidad a Distancia de Madrid.

Maria Heim is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Reed College and Harvard University under Charles Hallisey, Jambuvijaya, W. S. Karunatillake, and Nagin J. Shah. She served as Associate Professor at Amherst College (attested 2013–2020).

Maria Vasylieva, a Buddhist studies scholar, earned degrees from Uppsala University, the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine, Rangjung Yeshe Institute, and the International Buddhist College. In 2020, she became an Assistant Professor at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Maria Wilkins Smith worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Bryn Mawr College and the University of Pennsylvania under Roland Grubb Kent. Circa 1928–1948, she served at Temple University as Instructor and then Assistant Professor of Latin.

Marian Ury was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned her Ph.D. from the University of California, Berkeley. She served as a professor of East Asian languages and comparative literature at the University of California, Davis from 1969 to 1995.

Marianne Pieper studied at the Hamburger Hochschule für Wirtschaft und Politik and completed her Habilitation at Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg. She held professorial appointments at the University of Hamburg (1990–1994, 1996–2015) and the University of Kassel (1994–1996).

Marianne Winder specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of London, Nottingham, UCL, and SOAS under David Snellgrove, she held library posts at London and Wellcome, where she served as Curator (1970) and Consultant (1978).
Marianne Yaldiz is an archaeologist and Indologist. She served as Director of the Museum of Asian Art (attested 1997–2005) and Direktorin of the Museum für Indische Kunst (attested 2006).

Mariano José Saldanha was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sebastião Rodolfo Dalgado. He taught at Liceu Nacional Afonso de Albuquerque (1915–1929), the University of Lisbon (1929–1946), and was Subdirector at Instituto Superior de Ciências Sociais e Políticas (1929–1948).

Mariano Rampolla del Tindaro was an Indologist who studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University and under Oreste Nazari. In 1933, he was appointed professor of "Historia religionum in India et lingua Sanscrita" at the Pontifical Urban University.
Marie Brožová was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who completed her Ph.D. at Charles University under the supervision of Josef Zubatý.
Marie G. Wanek was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Pennsylvania under the instruction of Sengaku Mayeda.

Marie Gatellier was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Jean Boisselier and André Bareau. From circa 1980 to 1993, she served as Chargée de recherche at the National Centre for Scientific Research.

id: P:Marie-Jean-Léon Le Coq, Marquis d'Hervey de Saint-Denys
summary: Marie-Jean-Léon Le Coq, Marquis d'Hervey de Saint-Denys, was a Sinologist who studied under and later succeeded Stanislas Julien. He also taught Édouard Chavannes.
Marie-Stella Boussemart pursued studies under Samten Gyaltsen Karmay and Dagpo Rinpoche.
